Troubleshooting
Why these permissions?
Privacy
What does Pairline do?

It lets your iPhone use this Android phone\'s SIM card. Incoming calls and messages show up on your iPhone, and you can answer, reply, make calls and run USSD codes from there. This phone does the actual calling and texting, near your iPhone or, with Cloud mode, from home.
What do I need on the iPhone?

The Pairline app for iPhone (iOS 16 or later) and Bluetooth turned on. Nearby, the two phones need to be within Bluetooth range, usually the same room or a few rooms apart. With Cloud mode they can be anywhere with internet.
How do I pair?
On this phone, open Pair iPhone to show a code. On your iPhone, open Pairline, tap \"Pair a bridge phone\" and scan the code. The code works once and expires after 5 minutes.
Can I use my everyday Android phone?
Yes. A spare phone that only serves as the bridge is simplest, though: it can stay on the charger, and nothing else on it competes for battery or permissions.
Do I have to make Pairline my SMS app?
No. Android\'s own messaging app keeps working as usual and keeps all your messages. Pairline only relays them.
Why does the link sometimes drop?

Usually because Android or the phone\'s maker paused Pairline to save battery, or the phones were out of Bluetooth range. Allow background running in Keep Pairline running, and follow the tips for your phone.
Does Pairline drain the battery?
Not much. Bluetooth Low Energy is designed for this, and Pairline sleeps until something happens.
Why is there always a notification?
Android requires apps that run in the background to show one. It tells you whether your iPhone is connected, and it never shows message text or numbers.
How far apart can the phones be?
Nearby, about as far as a Bluetooth headset works: typically 10 to 30 meters indoors, less through thick walls. With Cloud mode, any distance.
My iPhone can\'t find this phone

Make sure both phones have Bluetooth turned on, that this app shows \"Waiting\" or \"Not paired\" without warnings, and that Pairline is open on the iPhone. If it still doesn\'t connect, turn Bluetooth off and on again on both phones.
Messages don\'t reach my iPhone
Make sure Text messages is allowed in Permissions and that the home screen says Connected. Messages that arrive while the link is down appear on the iPhone when it reconnects.
Where do I talk during a call?

On this Android phone, unless you set up Talk on iPhone (Settings › Talk on iPhone). Then calls you answer or place on the iPhone use the iPhone\'s microphone and speaker. It needs Android 11 or later, Wireless debugging (set up once in a few steps, no extra app) and both phones on the same Wi-Fi.
Why can\'t I use the keypad or mute from my iPhone?

Android only lets a few apps control a call in progress. Without help, Pairline can answer and end calls but not send keypad tones or mute. Set up Talk on iPhone (Settings › Talk on iPhone, Android 12 or later) and Pairline can do both.
Android says \"Restricted setting\"

Android 13 and later limit some permissions for apps installed outside an app store. Open App info for Pairline, tap ⋮ at the top and choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then allow the permission again.
Nearby devices (Bluetooth)
The link to your iPhone. Pairline announces itself only with an anonymous id, never your name or number, and doesn\'t use your location.
Text messages
To relay incoming messages to your iPhone, send the ones you write there, and load your history when the iPhone asks.
Phone calls and SIM cards
To notice calls, answer, decline, end and make them for your iPhone, run USSD codes, and show your SIMs and signal.
Call history

To show the caller\'s number (Android 12 and later only share it with this permission), your call history, and whether a call was missed or declined. When you delete calls on your iPhone, Pairline deletes them here too.
Contacts
To show caller names and your contacts on the iPhone. Writing contacts is a separate option, off unless you turn it on.
Notifications
For the status notification that Android requires for apps running in the background.
Battery optimization
Pairline asks Android, in Android\'s own window, not to pause it. You can change this anytime in Android\'s settings.
Where does my data go?

Only to your paired iPhone, end-to-end encrypted. Pairline has no servers. In Cloud mode it passes through your own iCloud, locked so only your two phones can read it. The only other connection is the daily update check on GitHub, which sends nothing about you and can be turned off in Settings.
What\'s in the diagnostics report?
Technical details such as versions, permissions and connection events. Phone numbers, emails, names, message text and keys are removed. You see the whole report before you choose to share it.
What happens when I unpair?
Both phones delete each other\'s key, so they can\'t talk to each other anymore. Your messages and contacts stay where they are on this phone.

Texts and codes still work. For calls from far away, turn on UPnP or NAT-PMP in your router\'s settings: it lets Pairline open, by itself, the one door your iPhone needs. Step by step for any router: Help › Allow calls from far away, in Pairline on your iPhone.

Texts and codes still work. For calls from far away, turn on UPnP on your provider\'s modem too, or put the modem in bridge mode. Step by step: Help › Allow calls from far away, in Pairline on your iPhone.

Texts and codes still work. Calls from far away need your own internet address, but your internet provider shares one among many homes (carrier-grade NAT): your router\'s internet (WAN) address starts with 100.64 to 100.127. No router setting helps here, so the router\'s UPnP list stays empty. Ask your provider for a public IPv4 address, or turn on IPv6 if they offer it; Pairline uses it by itself. More in Help.

Nearby or Cloud mode
Nearby or Cloud mode: which one do I need?

Nearby works by itself when the phones are near each other, for example with this phone in your bag or on your desk: they talk over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi. Cloud mode is for when this phone stays home, for example on its charger while you\'re at work or travelling: your iPhone then gets calls, texts and codes over the internet. Both can be on: at home the phones talk directly, and when you leave, Cloud mode takes over.
How do I turn on Cloud mode?

On your iPhone: when you pair, or later in Pairline\'s Settings. The iPhone gives this phone its own access to your iCloud, so there\'s no switch for it here. On this phone: keep it on its charger and home Wi-Fi, and let Pairline run in the background (Settings › Keep Pairline running). Settings › Cloud mode here shows whether everything is ready.
Texts arrive, but calls from far away don\'t work

Texts and codes reach your iPhone through iCloud. Talking on a call needs a straight way from your iPhone to this phone, through your home router. Most routers open it by themselves, with a setting called UPnP or NAT-PMP that is often on already. Settings › Cloud mode here says what\'s missing, and in Pairline on your iPhone, Help › Allow calls from far away has the steps for any router.
Does Cloud mode send my messages to a server?

Not to ours: Pairline has none. They go through your own iCloud as locked records that only your two phones can open; Apple can\'t read them. Calls go straight from your iPhone to this phone. When you turn Cloud mode off on the iPhone, its records in iCloud are deleted.
Do texts work while the phones are apart?

Yes, both ways, through your own iCloud (\"Via Cloud mode\"). A text from your iPhone goes out within a few seconds while this phone is on its charger, and within about 10 seconds on battery, because this phone checks iCloud that often while Cloud mode is on. Calls from far away need the direct connection through your home router.
Calls from far away say \"not possible\": the internet provider doesn\'t give this home its own address

Your internet provider shares one internet address among many homes (carrier-grade NAT), so nothing from outside can reach your router. To check: on your router\'s status page, its own internet (WAN) IPv4 address starts with 100.64 to 100.127, and a \"what\'s my IP\" website on the same Wi-Fi shows a different address. Pairline never asks such a website itself, so check by hand. Texts and codes still work through iCloud. For calls, ask your provider for a public IPv4 address (some call it a static or public IP), or turn on IPv6 in the router if they offer it (on a TP-Link: Advanced › Network › IPv6). Pairline uses IPv6 by itself. A 4G or 5G home router almost always gets such a shared address from the mobile operator: there a public address usually comes with a business or static-IP plan, and IPv6 is turned on in the router\'s APN settings (IPv4/IPv6) if the operator supports it.
UPnP is on, but the router\'s UPnP list is empty

With Cloud mode on and this phone on your home Wi-Fi, Pairline opens port 47830 through UPnP or NAT-PMP, and a Pairline entry shows in the router\'s list. If the list stays empty (for example \"Total Clients: 0\"), the router\'s own internet address isn\'t a public one, so Pairline opens nothing on purpose: nothing from outside could reach it. See the questions about the internet provider and the provider\'s modem.
My router sits behind the internet provider\'s modem

Then your router\'s own internet (WAN) address is a private one (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x or 172.16–31.x.x), and Settings › Cloud mode says another router sits in front of this one. Put the modem in bridge mode so your router gets the internet address, or turn on UPnP (or forward the port) on both the modem and the router.
What do I enter in the router for port forwarding?

Only needed if your router has no UPnP or NAT-PMP. Add a port forwarding rule (some routers call it a virtual server): protocol TCP, external (WAN) port 47830, internal (LAN) IP this phone\'s address on your home Wi-Fi, internal (LAN) port 47830. Settings › Cloud mode here shows this phone\'s address and the port in use. Reserve that address for this phone in the router\'s DHCP settings, using the device MAC shown there. Then, in Pairline on your iPhone, open Settings › Connection › Advanced › Port forwarding and enter your home\'s internet address or a DDNS name. Forward only 47830: 47820 is the nearby Wi-Fi link and stays inside your home. Only your paired iPhone can connect.
